items.question: Tell a new friend your favourite drink. Start with I.
items.feedback: Use subject + verb + object: I like tea.

items.question: Say where your friend lives. Start with She.
items.feedback: With she in the present simple, use lives. Near introduces the place.

items.question: Describe what the cat owns. Start with The cat and name the ball before the bed.
items.feedback: Each singular countable noun needs its own article: a ball and a bed. Use both a pieces.

items.question: Ask a friend about a weekend activity. Start with Would.
items.feedback: A polite invitation uses Would + subject + like to + base verb.

items.question: Describe your dinner plan. Start with We.
items.feedback: Be going to + base verb expresses a plan. Put tonight at the end here.

items.question: Compare two ways to travel. Start with This bus.
items.feedback: Use a comparative adjective + than to compare two things.

items.question: Explain your transport preference. Give the preference before the reason.
items.feedback: State the preference first, then use because + subject + verb to give a reason.

items.question: Describe what remote workers value. Start with People.
items.feedback: The relative clause who work remotely follows People and describes which people you mean.

items.question: Report an unfinished task. Start with I and end with yet.
items.feedback: Present perfect negative uses have not + past participle. Yet usually comes at the end.

items.question: The flight left before you reached the gate. Start with The flight.
items.feedback: Past perfect marks the earlier event; past simple marks the later arrival.

items.question: Explain the condition for a delivery. Put the result before the condition.
items.feedback: Provided that introduces a condition. The result clause comes first in this requested structure.

items.question: Ask politely about a delay. Start with Could you.
items.feedback: An indirect question uses statement order: why the delivery was delayed, not why was the delivery delayed.

items.question: Emphasise an unexpected problem. Start with Not only.
items.feedback: Initial Not only triggers auxiliary-subject inversion: did the launch fail.

items.question: Describe a missed chance to prevent a delay. Start with Had.
items.feedback: Had we identified is an inverted third conditional. The result uses could have + past participle.

items.question: Emphasise the evidence the team needs. Start with What.
items.feedback: A what-cleft highlights the focus after is; not introduces the contrasting alternative.

items.question: Express a recommendation as a formal necessity. Start with It.
items.feedback: The mandative subjunctive uses the base form be after it is essential that.

items.question: Describe two events in immediate succession. Start with Scarcely.
items.feedback: Initial Scarcely takes inversion and pairs with when: Scarcely had ... when ...

items.question: State the main issue while rejecting a distraction. Start with The issue.
items.feedback: Not so much X as Y shifts emphasis from X to the more relevant issue Y.

items.question: Suggest a film outing. Start with How about and end with the day.
items.feedback: How about takes an -ing form when suggesting an activity.

items.question: Suggest a meeting. Put the cafe and its location before the time.
items.feedback: Could + base verb makes a suggestion. Near the lake identifies which cafe.

items.question: Accept the plan, then say goodbye. Start with Sounds good.
items.feedback: I'll is I will. See you then refers back to the agreed time.

items.question: Report yesterday's finished task. Put the time first.
items.feedback: Use the past simple for a finished task: fixed. The time comes first here.

items.question: State today's next task. Put the time first.
items.feedback: Will + base verb states your next action. The object follows add.

items.question: Report that nothing is blocking you. Put the time last.
items.feedback: No + plural noun expresses absence. Right now makes the status current.

items.question: Explain the risk created by the deadline. Start with The Friday deadline.
items.feedback: Name the constraint as the subject, then describe its consequence with creates.

items.question: Offer a quality trade-off. Put the result before the if-clause.
items.feedback: The result is protecting quality; the if-clause states the required scope reduction.

items.question: Propose a smaller delivery. Start with I propose and put the date last.
items.feedback: Propose takes an -ing form. Name the deliverable before the delivery date.
